question: What is the Commission required to do with the National Register of Voters according to the Electoral Act?
answer: Section 9(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026 requires the Commission to compile, maintain, and update, on a continuous basis, a National Register of Voters. This register must include the names of all persons entitled to vote in any Federal, State, Local Government or Federal Capital Territory Area Council election, and must contain disability status disaggregated by type of disability [act-s9-0].

question: Where and in what formats must the Commission keep the Register of Voters?
answer: Section 9(2) states that the Commission shall keep the Register of Voters in its National Headquarters and other locations it determines. It must be kept both in electronic format in its central database and in manual, printed, paper-based record or hard copy format [act-s9-0].

question: What documents must an applicant present when registering under the continuous registration system?
answer: Section 10(2) specifies that each applicant shall appear in person at the registration venue with any of the following documents: a Nigerian birth certificate, a Nigerian passport, or a National Identification Number (NIN) [act-s10-0]. Section 10(3) further requires the Commission to make available to every political party the names and addresses of each person registered during that year within 60 days after each year [act-s10-0].

question: What happens to the Register of Voters when a general election is notified, and how is the register used for bye-elections?
answer: Section 10(4) provides that when a general election is notified, the current official Register of Voters certified by the Commission shall be the official voters' register for those elections [act-s10-0]. Section 10(5) adds that for bye-elections, the official voters' register shall be the existing current register relating to the senatorial district or constituency concerned [act-s10-0].

question: Can members of the public object to registration officers, and what is the effect if no objection is raised?
answer: Section 11(2) allows any person to raise an objection against any officer during the registration or updating exercise. Section 11(2) also states that failure to raise such an objection shall not vitiate the register [act-s11-0].

question: What restrictions apply to registration officers regarding political party membership and their duties?
answer: Section 11(1) requires that registration officers appointed by the Commission shall not be members of any political party. Section 11(3) further provides that these officers shall perform functions as specified by the Commission and shall not be subject to the direction or control of any person or authority other than the Commission [act-s11-0].

question: What are the legal qualifications for a person to be registered as a voter?
answer: Section 12(1)(a) and (b) require that a person be a citizen of Nigeria and have attained the age of 18 years. Sections 12(1)(c) through (e) further require that the person be ordinarily resident, work in, and originate from the Local Government, Area Council or Ward covered by the registration centre, present themselves for registration, and not be subject to any legal incapacity to vote [act-s12-0].

question: What penalty does the law impose for registering more than once at the same registration centre?
answer: Section 12(2) prohibits a person from registering in more than one registration centre or more than once in the same centre.
